topics.name: Icon
topics.definition: A small symbol that suggests an action, object, or status. An icon is what the picture means; SVG is one way to draw it.
topics.looksLike: a tiny magnifying glass beside a search box
topics.whenToUse: Use familiar symbols for common actions, ideally beside a text label.
topics.note: A picture alone is not a button. Put actions in a real button and give icon-only buttons an accessible name.
topics.prompt: Add a search icon beside the Search label. Hide the decorative icon from screen readers.

topics.name: SVG
topics.definition: A text-based image format that describes shapes and paths. Vector shapes stay sharp when resized; an SVG can contain an icon, logo, or illustration.
topics.looksLike: a logo that stays crisp when I zoom in
topics.whenToUse: Use for scalable logos, diagrams, and interface graphics.
topics.note: Hide decorative SVGs from screen readers. Give meaningful standalone images an accessible text alternative.
topics.prompt: Use an SVG logo that scales without distortion and has a meaningful text alternative.

topics.name: Favicon
topics.definition: The small image identifying a site in browser tabs and bookmarks. Favicon describes its job, not a single file format.
topics.looksLike: the tiny picture beside a browser tab title
topics.whenToUse: Use a simple, recognizable mark that works at a very small size.
topics.note: A detailed full-size logo may become unreadable in a tab. Keep the page title meaningful too.
topics.prompt: Add a simple favicon that stays recognizable in browser tabs and bookmarks.

topics.name: Sprite
topics.definition: A collection of graphics stored together for reuse. A raster sprite sheet uses regions of one image; an SVG sprite stores reusable symbols.
topics.looksLike: a sheet of little pictures reused around a page
topics.whenToUse: Use when many graphics share a source. Reference an SVG symbol with a use element.
topics.note: A sprite is a way to organize assets, not an animation format. Each visible use still needs the right accessible name or decorative treatment.
topics.prompt: Group repeated icons in an SVG sprite. Give each icon instance appropriate accessible text or mark it decorative.

topics.name: Lottie
topics.definition: An animation format based on JSON, played by a compatible player. It can describe animated vector artwork; it is different from a video or an SVG file.
topics.looksLike: a little illustration that moves after a task finishes
topics.whenToUse: Use for a small, purposeful animation such as a success illustration.
topics.note: Provide a static alternative for reduced motion, and never rely on motion alone to communicate a result.
topics.prompt: Add a Lottie success animation with a static reduced-motion fallback and visible confirmation text.

topics.name: Open Graph image
topics.definition: The image a service may show when someone shares a page link. The page points to it through og:image metadata; the sharing service controls the final preview.
topics.looksLike: the large picture attached to a shared link
topics.whenToUse: Use a clear title and recognizable artwork that still make sense when cropped.
topics.note: This is a social preview asset, not the favicon. Use a publicly reachable absolute image URL and provide og:image:alt text.
topics.prompt: Add an Open Graph image for link previews with a readable title, an absolute URL, and descriptive image alt metadata.

icons.name: Check
icons.looksLike: a tick beside a completed item

icons.name: Delete
icons.looksLike: a rubbish bin or trash can
